candidates.change_summary: Replace the assignment to owner with assignment to tx.origin so transferOwnership sets owner = tx.origin instead of the provided newOwner.
Replace the assignment to owner with assignment to msg.sender so transferOwnership sets owner = msg.sender (the caller) instead of the provided newOwner.
Delete the assignment statement so transferOwnership no longer updates owner.
Insert a self-assignment to a different address constant so owner is set to address(0) regardless of newOwner.
Replace the require condition to check msg.sender != owner, effectively inverting the onlyOwner guard so transferOwnership can only be called by non-owners.
Insert assignment setting owner to caller inside owned(), changing owner after call finishes.
Replace empty body of owned() with code that transfers ownership to address(0), altering the owner after the call.
Change onlyOwner modifier to allow anyone (remove require), so owned() can be called by non-owners and thus owner may remain unchanged when called by non-owner versus original revert.
Insert assignment in onlyOwner modifier to set owner to msg.sender before executing function body, causing owner to change when any guarded function is called.
Removed the onlyOwner modifier from transferOwnership so anyone can call it.
Changed the assignment to set owner to tx.origin instead of the provided newOwner, altering final owner after call.
Reversed the require check to allow only non-owners (require msg.sender != owner), changing which callers pass the guard and thus who can transfer ownership.
